chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Road audiences danced more than New Yorkers
summary: Road crowds danced all night since the band was there only once; the Savoy's two bands alternated set lengths.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: How about the dancing? When does the dancing come in and also when you went on the road? Did the audiences -- the crowds on the road dance more than the New York audiences or...?
No, they didn't dance. They dance more, yeah. They danced more because for the simple reason that (inaudible) understand that you're only in town for that one night. And people danced all night long.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

They just sitting down. Well, you know, like the Savoy Ballroom was so big you had a lot of people sitting down and you had a lot of people dancing. They be sitting down drinking and eating and then dancing all night long. That's why you had two bands up there. See, the Savoy Ballroom had two bands. Time one band would stop -- I'd be on forty-five minutes, the other band would be on thirty minutes, (inaudible) twenty minutes. We always played five or ten minutes more than the --
See, we always played the Set, the longer (inaudible) Savoy Sultans played (inaudible). Twenty minutes or something like that. And we play thirty-five minutes, .something like that, you know.
